data.title: Prototype surface placement in supported AR
data.summary: One metre-scaled model and an AR-capable device/browser. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Three.js documents enabling a WebXR VR rendering session.
The WebXR Hit Test draft describes placement against detected physical surfaces; device support and feature permissions are required.

prerequisites: An authorized Three.js / WebXR environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: One metre-scaled model and an AR-capable device/browser.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent ar placement workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: One metre-scaled model and an AR-capable device/browser. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Check the browser's supported immersive-ar and required hit-test features before starting
Use the platform's documented hit-test path and place a single anchored candidate
Show a manual fallback and test scale, reset and session exit on the real device

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned prototype surface placement in supported ar candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Unsupported devices receive a usable fallback
Reset removes the placed candidate without leaving duplicate anchors
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: WebXR VR support does not imply AR hit-test support; this AR procedure needs platform-specific documentation and testing.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: A desktop emulator cannot establish physical-device tracking quality.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me prototype surface placement in supported ar in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: One metre-scaled model and an AR-capable device/browser. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Unsupported devices receive a usable fallback; Reset removes the placed candidate without leaving duplicate anchors. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
